baseline.description: A perturbation changes expression by the sum of its genes' single-gene changes in training (additive model).

lineage.hypothesis: Warm start: the best model of run norman_control_replogle_w4_r0 (EXP_0198, visible 0.6423) is the starting point of this run.
For pairs, the prior network edge weight between the two target genes predicts non-additive response.
Using Euclidean distance between the external Replogle response vectors of perturbation targets (rather than Jaccard similarity of target sets) improves prediction of unseen perturbations.
The functional similarity between the target genes of a perturbation (e.g., via gene-set overlap) predicts response magnitude and specificity.
The number of transcription factors shared between the target genes of a pair perturbation is predictive of response.
Refine the ridge penalty around alpha=0.01 for the best model (EXP_0092).
The number of gene sets containing both target genes of a pair perturbation improves prediction of pair responses beyond existing functional-coherence features.
Refine the ridge penalty around alpha=0.01 for the best model (EXP_0126).
Refine the ridge penalty around alpha=0.0033 for the best model (EXP_0134).
The number of neighbors k in similar_pert_external_response_knn_e52 can be tuned to improve pearson_delta. [sweep feature_params.similar_pert_external_response_knn_e52.k=20]
Refine the ridge penalty around alpha=100 for the best model (EXP_0170).
The rank of gene g's control expression among all genes, conditioned on whether g is a target or not, captures perturbation-specific regulatory potential beyond raw control mean.
Refine the ridge penalty around alpha=0.01 for the best model (EXP_0176).
The product of pair_target_shared_tf_count_e83_e92 and pair_target_shared_pathway_count_e126 captures synergy between regulatory and pathway overlap.
The shortest path length between the two targets in the prior network (or a large constant if disconnected) predicts pair perturbation synergy.
For a perturbation p, the specificity of each target's gene-set membership (e.g., inverse of number of gene sets containing the target) modulates the response of gene g.
Refine the ridge penalty around alpha=0.01 for the best model (EXP_0243).
The product of the absolute external response of the target and the control expression of gene g captures an interaction between target effect strength and baseline expression.
The asymmetry in gene-set membership overlap between the two targets of a pair perturbation predicts response magnitude.
Drop external_direct_replogle2022_k562_e16 from the best model (EXP_0289) to test whether it still earns its place.
A low-dimensional random projection of the external Replogle response vector, interacted with target membership, captures complex target-specific patterns not seen by individual features.
The Jaccard index between the gene set memberships of the perturbation targets and the top differentially expressed genes in the training response is predictive.
Refine the ridge penalty around alpha=0.01 for the best model (EXP_0352).
Removing features with near-zero coefficients (prior_network_edge_e8, target_gene_set_specificity_e243, target_response_pathway_overlap_e352) improves generalization by reducing noise.
The product of the additive single-gene response (additive_singles_e15) and the prior network edge between pair targets (pair_target_prior_edge_e34) captures synergy for pair perturbations.
A random projection of gene g's external Replogle delta vector across perturbations captures a compressed signature of its response profile, improving prediction beyond target-specific features.
The square of additive_singles_e15 for pair perturbations captures saturation or amplification effects, improving prediction when single-gene effects are large.
Refine the ridge penalty around alpha=0.01 for the best model (EXP_0456).
After removing near-zero features, the optimal ridge penalty may change; sweeping alpha can find a better value. [sweep alpha_grid=0.001]
Refine the ridge penalty around alpha=0.001 for the best model (EXP_0481).
Refine the ridge penalty around alpha=0.0006 for the best model (EXP_0488).
A low-dimensional random projection of the target gene's control expression profile (across all genes) captures latent regulatory state and predicts delta.
A finer sweep of ridge alpha around 0.01 may improve performance slightly. [sweep alpha_grid=0.005]
Refine the ridge penalty around alpha=0.005 for the best model (EXP_0537).
Refine the ridge penalty around alpha=0.00165 for the best model (EXP_0544).
The number of shared PPI neighbors between gene g and the perturbation's target genes is predictive of the expression change of g.
Refine the ridge penalty around alpha=0.01 for the best model (EXP_0567).
Refine the ridge penalty around alpha=0.0033 for the best model (EXP_0584).
Refine the ridge penalty around alpha=0.00198 for the best model (EXP_0588).
The product of additive_singles_e15 and external_response_times_control_expr_e279 captures synergistic effects between internal and external response estimates, improving prediction.

The product of target_set_functional_coherence_e74 (specificity of target's gene set membership) and the sign-corrected external Replogle delta of the target improves prediction by modulating the target's effect strength.
The specificity of the perturbation's target set to a small number of pathways (measured by entropy of gene-set membership counts) predicts delta.
Refine the ridge penalty around alpha=0.01 for the best model (EXP_0642).
The product of pair_target_shared_tf_count_e83_e92 and target_set_pathway_entropy_e642 captures the interplay between regulatory overlap and functional diversity of targets.
Removing pair_target_shared_pathway_count_e126 from the best model improves or maintains performance by reducing noise.
Refine the ridge penalty around alpha=0.01 for the best model (EXP_0694).
Refine the ridge penalty around alpha=0.0033 for the best model (EXP_0717).

most_useful_features.description: Average training delta of the k perturbations whose target gene sets are most Jaccard-similar to p's targets.
Average training delta of the k perturbations whose external Replogle target response vectors are closest (Euclidean) to p's external response vector.
Dot product between target loading vectors and gene loading vectors on top control PCs, weighted by PC variance explained.
Mean control-expression correlation between gene g and the target gene(s) of perturbation p.
Percentile rank of gene g's control mean expression, interacted with target membership.
Dot product between a fixed random projection of gene g's sign-corrected external Replogle delta and the average projected vector of the perturbation's target genes.
Element-wise product of target_level_e11 and external_direct_replogle2022_k562_e16.
Mean control expression of PPI neighbors of perturbation targets (excluding the targets), projected through a fixed random Gaussian matrix to k dimensions.
